title: Your First React App
description: Build a simple React application and understand how components work together.

data.text: Now that you understand JSX, let's build your first React application. We'll create a simple component that receives data through props and responds to events.
A React component is a reusable piece of UI. Let's create a simple component that displays a greeting.

data.title: Simple Component

data.text: Let's build a component that accepts data and responds to user interaction. This introduces the concept of props and event handling.

data.title: Counter Component

items: **count state**: Holds the current count value initialized to 0
**setCount**: Function to update the state value
**onClick**: Event handler that calls setCount when clicked
**{count}**: Displays the current state value in the UI

data.text: Let's enhance our component with additional interactive features using event handlers.

data.title: Enhanced Counter
data.content: Counter with increment, decrement, and reset

data.text: To see your component, you need to render it in the main App component.

data.title: App Component
Component Naming
data.text: React components must start with a capital letter. This is how React distinguishes between HTML elements and custom components.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Components are reusable pieces of UI
Component state manages data that changes over time
Event handlers update state and trigger re-renders
Components are composed together to build complex UIs
data.takeaway: You've built your first React app! Next, let's dive deeper into components and props.
